p: Agur the son of Jakeh: Who was an excellent man in virtue and knowledge in the time of Solomon.
Ithiel and Ucal: Who were Agur's scholars or friends.
senseless than any man: In this he declares his great humility who would not attribute any wisdom to himself but all to God.
heaven: Meaning, to know the secrets of God, as though he would say, "None".
things have I required of thee: He makes this request to God.
Who is the LORD: Meaning, that they who put their trust in their riches forget God and that by too much wealth men have an opportunity to the same.
and thou be found guilty: In accusing him without cause.
daughters: The leach has two forks in her tongue, which here he calls her two daughters, by which she sucks the blood, and is never satisfied: even so, the covetous extortioners are insatiable.
of the valley shall pick it: Which hunt in the valley for carrion.
wipeth her mouth: She has her desires, and later counterfeits as though she were an honest woman.
a servant when he reigneth: These commonly abuse the state to which they are called.
heir to her mistress: Who is married to her master after the death of her mistress.
wise: They contain great doctrine and wisdom.
with her hands: If man is not able to compass these common things by his wisdom, we cannot attribute wisdom to man, but folly.
upon thy mouth: Make a stay and continue not in doing evil.
